leads.candidate: Penang Botanic Gardens cannonball trees (Couroupita guianensis), about 10 planted 1886 near the main entrance
leads.reason: NST 2021 says about 135 years old, from Brazil; ensemble along the entrance path, individual trunks not identified, no register, no coordinates. Fold into one entry only if one trunk can be pinned. Entry to the gardens is free.

leads.candidate: Penang Botanic Gardens upas ipoh (Antiaris toxicaria), three towering trees
leads.reason: Blog only (thepoisonhunter.blogspot.com 2021), author's estimate of at least 100 years, no coordinates. Not a source.

leads.candidate: Bodhi tree at Shree Muniswarar temple, Waterfall Road
leads.reason: Areca Books 2015 news piece only: about the age of the hundred-year-old temple, no measurement, no coordinate. Temple precinct would need a pin.

leads.candidate: Century-old angsana and rain trees on York Road, Waterfall Road and Macalister Road with MBPP identity cards (2013)
leads.reason: Areca Books 2015 piece says MBPP issued cards with species, serial number and location; no list published. Penang Tree Inventory System (PeTIS) holds it; ask MBPP. 314 century-old large trees in MBPP area need trunk inspections (The Star, 5 Jun 2024). Many are being felled for safety, so check alive per tree.

leads.candidate: Mengkundur tree, Bukit Mertajam (probably Malaysia's tallest, The Star 23 Nov 2020)
leads.reason: Mainland Seberang Perai, not a day trip from George Town on a labelled basis; not examined beyond the headline. Look at it with a Seberang Perai pass.

leads.candidate: Sentang (Melia excelsa) said to be Penang's oldest street tree since 1820, per 2010 coverage of Heritage Trees of Penang (FRIM clipping)
leads.reason: Location not named in anything fetched (FRIM PDF 404); the Areca article does not contain it. Need the book (Gardner, Sidisunthorn, Lai 2011, Areca Books) for the location.
